issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'אֶת רֶגֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱמַדְתִּי לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם' means 'the foot of Israel from the land which I have appointed for your fathers' — the land is appointed for the fathers, not 'from the land established by your fathers' (從你們父所立的田地). The Chinese rendering reverses the relationship: it says the land was established by the fathers, whereas the Hebrew says God appointed it for the fathers.

The Hebrew 'וְהַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים' lists three items: 'the Torah, the statutes, and the judgments' (律法、律例、典章). The Chinese renders '律法、律法與審判' — the second item 'חֻקִּים' (statutes/律例) is omitted and replaced by a repetition of '律法' (Torah). This is a substantive omission of a distinct legal category.
